name: iocraft
tagline: React-style declarative TUIs and CLI output for Rust

license.notes: Dual-licensed at the user's option (GitHub reports Apache-2.0).

adoption.downloads: 187k all-time, 53k in the last 90 days (crates.io); 15 reverse dependencies
adoption.summary: Small but real adoption in Rust developer tooling.

maintainability.bus_factor: low: ccbrown has ~194 of the commits; next human contributor 9

architecture.summary: React/Dioxus-style component model in Rust: an element! macro declares trees of components (View, Text, TextInput, …), #[component] functions receive props and Hooks (use_state, use_future, use_context, use_terminal_events), and the runtime re-renders on state change. Layout is flexbox via taffy. The same tree can be printed once to any output (logs, non-TTY), rendered as an inline animated region, or run fullscreen; props and context can be passed by reference to avoid cloning.
key_points: Static print, inline render_loop, or fullscreen
Works on Unix and Windows terminals
Elements can be rendered to a string (print/to_string) for non-TTY output

agent_usability.integration_effort: Same as any library: the app author builds a control channel.
agent_usability.readback: Elements can be rendered to a string; otherwise screen scraping.
agent_usability.summary: Pleasant declarative Rust API, no agent surface.

score_notes.ui_as_data: Declarative macro in Rust; not serializable
score_notes.maturity: Used in production by moonrepo and devenv, small ecosystem

steelman: iocraft is the answer for Rust developers who find ratatui's immediate mode too low-level: you write components with props, state and hooks like React, lay them out with flexbox (taffy), and get one tree that can be printed to a log, animated inline in a CLI or run as a fullscreen app on Unix and Windows. That inline/print-first design suits developer tools — which is why moonrepo's moon and proto and cachix's devenv use it — and the API is small, readable and dual-licensed MIT/Apache.
weaknesses: Small widget set compared with ratatui
Rust's ownership rules limit how React-like it can be (HN discussion)

relation_to_scene.overlap: Rust, declarative component tree, flexbox layout, inline-or-fullscreen rendering.
relation_to_scene.scene_reinvents: Little — scene's declarative tree is data, not a macro DSL; component vocabulary overlaps.
borrow: Inline (non-fullscreen) render mode and print-once mode for one-shot scene output
taffy as a flexbox engine if scene needs richer layout
relation_to_scene.gap_left: Everything agent-facing: serializable UI, socket control, readback, streams, pixels, hot-swap, time travel.
relation_to_scene.verdict_why: A code-first Rust alternative to ratatui; nothing scene would build on, only minor ideas to borrow.
